corrections.caveats: Not faster than the best C entries on HttpArena's scored HTTP/1.1 profiles: at baseline-4096 libreactorng (4,377,377) and libioma (4,255,834) are ahead (0.96x, 0.98x), and limited-conn-4096 is a tie (1.01x over libioma 2,707,029, mongoose 2,701,933 and libreactorng 2,685,717). The only clear win over C is pipelined-4096 (1.26x libreactorng), which is reference-only in HttpArena's composite score (site/content/docs/scoring/composite-score.md). The entry is a minimal server written for the suite (meta.json lists no maintainers; it is not tokio project code): it routes only /pipeline and /delay and answers every other path with the a+b sum, sends no Date or Server header, and runs on epoll while libreactorng and libioma use io_uring. Bytes per response (derived from page data, bandwidth divided by req/s) are 62.9 at baseline-4096 against 108.7 for libreactorng (which sends a per-second cached Date header, per vanilla's docs/PERF_GAP_ANALYSIS.md), 85.8 for libioma, 72.5 for mongoose, 98.2 for h2o and 135.4 for nginx; at pipelined-4096 it writes 61.4 bytes per response against libreactorng's 106.2 (3.36 GB/s against 4.61 GB/s), so the pipelined ratio tracks smaller responses. The ratios over nginx, h2o and mongoose compare a minimal handler with full servers that write larger headers. Does not generalise to hyper or axum (hyper 3,003,360 req/s at baseline-4096). Other non-C entries are faster than this Rust entry at baseline-4096 (zix 4,442,329 and zeemo 4,422,489 in Zig, minima-sync 4,386,544 in C#). Each number is the best of 3 runs of 5 s with the server limited to 32 cores / 64 threads; results files are undated and rows come from different runs (tokio.json last written 2026-08-30, libreactorng.json 2026-09-07, per git history). The C/C++ rows are built -O3 -march=native (nginx, libreactorng, libioma, mongoose; libioma and mongoose also with LTO) or clang CMake Release -march=native (h2o); the Drogon entry builds only its handler against the unpinned drogonframework/drogon:latest image, so the Drogon ratio (2.07x) is weaker evidence than the nginx, h2o, libreactorng and libioma ratios.
corrections.why_faster: No language-level mechanism shown. The entry uses per-core current_thread tokio runtimes with SO_REUSEPORT (no work stealing), TCP_NODELAY, one batched write per read and a minimal hand-rolled parser (frameworks/tokio/README.md, src/main.rs), which is the same shared-nothing design as the C engines. The margins that exist come from smaller responses (no Date or Server header) and minimal routing; on the scored profiles the best C io_uring engines are level or ahead.

notes: All quoted numbers verified against the HttpArena JSON files; tier A kept on the HttpArena precedent. Corrected: runs are best of 3, not one; same_algorithm set false (62.9 bytes per response with no Date or Server header against 108.7 for libreactorng and 135.4 for nginx, epoll against io_uring, routing limited to /pipeline). corrections.caveats: The json-comp ratios (9.6x over userver, 22x over Drogon) time a response cache: write_json_gzip in main.v keeps complete gzipped responses keyed by (count, m), compresses once on the first miss and appends the cached bytes on every hit, while HttpArena's json-comp rules forbid pre-compressed caches for standard and tuned entries (vanilla is an 'engine' entry, which has no rules) and the C++ rows compress per request. vanilla's rate there is 2.7x the next entry (zix, which compresses per request). No C engine or nginx runs json-comp. The json-tls body is partly pre-serialized: each item's JSON except total is rendered once at startup into a prefix string, so per request vanilla formats one integer per item and copies prefixes, whereas nginx's infrastructure rules require full per-request serialization; TLS is Mbed TLS (C, patched to cache the RSA signing context) with kTLS record offload in the kernel. static-tls and pipelined are reference-only profiles. At baseline-4096 the entry trails libreactorng (0.98x) and is level with libioma (1.01x) and at limited-conn it ties libreactorng and libioma, so on the scored HTTP/1.1 profiles vanilla matches but does not beat the best C engines. The vanilla-epoll entry is slower at baseline-4096 (3,985,550) and at limited-conn-4096 (1,021,750). V compiles to C (gcc -O3 -flto), so this is a V-generated C server against hand-written C servers, not a different code generator. Bytes per response at baseline-4096 (derived from page data, bandwidth divided by req/s): vanilla 102.0 (Server and Connection headers, no Date), nginx 135.4, Drogon 134.4, libreactorng 108.7, h2o 98.2, libioma 85.8, mongoose 72.5; at baseline-h2c-256 vanilla-epoll writes 43.2 bytes per response against agensio's 25.9. The h2c row comes from the -gc none build, which never frees memory. Each number is the best of 3 runs of 5 s with the server limited to 32 cores / 64 threads; results files are undated and rows come from different runs (vanilla-io_uring.json last written 2026-10-02, vanilla-epoll.json 2026-10-11, agensio.json 2026-10-06, libreactorng.json 2026-09-07, per git history). The vanilla entries are maintained by the vanilla author (meta.json maintainers: enghitalo). The vanilla README publishes no throughput numbers against C servers; docs/PERF_GAP_ANALYSIS.md treats libreactorng, zeemo and tokio as the faster reference servers. The Drogon entry builds only its handler against the unpinned drogonframework/drogon:latest image and userver uses a prebuilt v3.2 image, so those ratios are weaker evidence than the nginx, h2o, libreactorng and libioma ratios.
corrections.why_faster: Server design and C libraries, not V: an io_uring runtime with one worker per CPU and SO_REUSEPORT, handlers that return raw response bytes, JSON items pre-rendered into prefixes at startup (HttpArena meta.json, main.v), TLS from Mbed TLS (C) with kTLS, and gzip from miniz (C) behind a response cache for json-comp. V itself compiles to C built by gcc -O3 -flto.

notes: Numbers verified, tier A kept, verdict downgrade because the claim was overstated: the json-comp 9.6x and 22x wins time cached gzipped responses (main.v write_json_gzip compresses once per (count, m) and replays the bytes), so they are struck as invalid evidence (wazero cache-hit precedent). Shortcomings to record: on scored HTTP/1.1 profiles it only ties the best C engines (0.98x libreactorng at baseline-4096, 1.00x at limited-conn); json-tls beaten by agensio (0.89x) and partly pre-serialized; TLS is Mbed TLS (C) with kTLS; static-tls and pipelined are reference-only; V compiles to C; vendor-maintained entries; cross-run rows. Metadata confirmed: MIT, 41 stars, last commit 2026-10-12, not a fork, not archived.
